assessment.assessment: Film and literature courses support interpretation, while history and art courses supply context. The evidence does not establish a cumulative sequence in music theory, aural skills, score analysis, musical performance analysis, or historical repertoire.

Media & Race and Native American Histories use music within specific cultural and historical inquiries. Media Archaeology, documentary and qualitative methods extend interpretation of sound and culture. These contributions are bounded and cannot sustain a programme in musical traditions, ethnomusicology or popular music.

Perception, higher cognitive functions, statistics, signal analysis and programming provide transferable methods. They do not supply a progression in music cognition, rhythm, musical listening experiments or computational music research.

academicConstruction: Tested an arts, cultural-history and social inquiry trial using directly relevant examples of music in Native American Histories and Media & Race, alongside sound in film, media history, documentary and creative work. The second trial pairs sensory and higher cognition, mathematical signal analysis, statistics and computing with sound-related media. General perceptual methods and Fourier and sampling concepts are real preparation, but no documented course sequence supports research into musical rhythm, listening, musical memory or analysis of music datasets. The arts trial lacks musical historiography, the study of repertoire, harmony and ethnomusicological progression. Full 24-course scheduling succeeds for both. The finding is academic.
distinctness: Two different disciplinary trial emphases were tested. Neither meets comparability and neither is selected
